question: Should existing user-managed daily dreaming markdown and `DREAMS.md` files above 16 MiB become a hard runtime failure, and if so what supported recovery path should users receive?
rationale: The cap prevents unbounded reads, but it changes the runtime contract for previously valid workspace files; source and tests cannot determine whether that upgrade impact is acceptable.

options.title: Require an upgrade-safe recovery path
options.body: Keep the bounded reader but add a clear supported remediation or migration path before turning oversized existing files into a hard dreaming failure.

options.title: Accept the hard 16 MiB limit
options.body: Approve the fail-fast policy as intentional and document the limit plus the user-visible recovery steps for oversized workspace files.

options.title: Defer the cap
options.body: Pause this PR until the memory-file size policy is decided in the broader dreaming storage design.

recommendation.title: Require an upgrade-safe recovery path
recommendation.body: Keep the bounded reader but add a clear supported remediation or migration path before turning oversized existing files into a hard dreaming failure.
